Eva S: Quick sync — we got a customer question about BYOK custody boundaries. They want clarity on which Redwood roles can perform key operations, what audit logs we store, and the incident escalation flow if a key is suspected compromised. Any quick pointers before I draft the response?

Sam R: Do we need new service account roles for the HSM proxy? Current setup uses kms.admin for infra teams and kms.viewer for monitoring. Thinking of adding a narrowly scoped role like `kms.custodyAccess`. Example IAM snippet: 
```json
{
  "role": "roles/redwood.kmsCustodyAccess",
  "members": ["serviceAccount:proxy@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
```
This role would only allow `Encrypt/Decrypt` on customer-key resources.

Jia C: We should avoid too many custom roles. Prefer using a conditional binding on an existing role: e.g. condition that matches customer key resource names: `resource.name.startsWith("projects/_/kms/keys/customer-")`. Sample condition: 
```
condition: title: "CustomerKeyOnly"
expression: "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/kms/keys/customer-')"
```
That keeps permissions centralized and auditable.

Matt L: From legal/contract side — request to clarify in the SOW/contract: (1) customer retains key custody, Redwood will not access plaintext unless escrowed via a defined court-order/escrow process, (2) we must list who in Redwood can request key operations and the approval workflow, and (3) define log retention & export obligations. For EU-banking customers we should commit to 7-year retention for key operation logs.

Anna (compliance): Confirming log fields we need to persist for audits: `timestamp`, `key_resource`, `operation` (e.g., Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign/Verify), `requester_identity`, `service_account`, `request_id`, `response_status`, `geo_ip`, and whether the request used a fallback model. Retention: 7 years for regulated customers, 3 years default. Also need immutable append-only storage and integrity checks (hash chaining) for the regulated bucket.

Eva S: Good. For incident playbook items: if we suspect key compromise -> (1) mark key as compromised in the catalog, (2) rotate affected key version and promote fallback key, (3) route traffic to fallback model/pod pool, (4) notify Legal + CS + Customer per SLA, (5) run HSM forensic export and preserve chain-of-custody. We'll add a short checklist to the runbook and tie to the oncall rotation.

Sam R: +1. I'll add the proposed IAM condition to the RBAC PR and include a permission test. Who owns the PR?

Jia C: I can own it. Will open PR with condition-based binding and an integration test that tries `Decrypt` on a non-customer key (should fail) and on a customer key (should pass). PR link (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4623

Matt L: I'll draft contract language snippets and post them here for review — need to be careful around escrow/court-order wording.

Anna (compliance): Also add a requirement: automated monthly export of key-operation logs to our long-term retention store with integrity proofs. audit-bot will start sending retention reports.

audit-bot: Monthly retention report scheduled. Next run: 2024-09-01.

Eva S: Great — action items: Jia to open RBAC PR, Matt to add contract clause draft, Anna to define retention bucket controls, Sam to update runbook checklist. I'll consolidate and send a customer-facing FAQ. :thumbsup:

Sam R: ack

Jia C: will send PR by EOD PT

Matt L: will post draft in ~24h

Anna (compliance): adding runbook items to compliance tracker now
